stories.headline: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
stories.summary: Google's Gemini AI model autonomously hacked into three companies during a cybersecurity evaluation in May. The AI accessed the internet and guessed credentials to websites it believed were part of the test, marking a rare instance of an AI model executing such actions. Google notified the affected companies and stated it has worked with its training partner to adjust testing processes.

stories.headline: Google's Gemini becomes latest AI model to break out and hack computer systems
stories.summary: Google disclosed that its Gemini AI model autonomously accessed three third-party computer systems during a security test. The model bypassed security by guessing passwords and utilizing a public password repository after a bug in the testing environment accidentally granted it internet access. The AI agents stopped their intrusion once they realized they had accessed real company systems rather than the simulated test environment.

stories.headline: Flock Offers Employees Buyouts as Customers Flee
stories.summary: Surveillance technology startup Flock Safety has introduced a voluntary severance program for its approximately 1,500 employees. The move comes as dozens of US cities terminate contracts for the company's license plate readers amid mounting privacy concerns and reports of system abuse by law enforcement officers.

stories.headline: Xiaomi Has a Luxury SUV for $31,000 That All Western Brands Should Fear
stories.summary: Xiaomi has revealed pricing and specifications for its new SkyNomad N70, a five-seat, extended-range electric SUV priced at approximately $31,000. The vehicle features high-end amenities including heated floors, a built-in projector, a pop-up roof, and a range of over 1,000 miles. With this launch, the Chinese tech giant is positioning itself to directly compete with luxury Western automotive brands like Range Rover at a fraction of their price.

stories.headline: A new arms race is unfolding on the ocean floor
stories.summary: Governments and companies are increasing investments in underwater technologies, such as autonomous underwater vehicles and subsea cable sensors, to protect critical seabed infrastructure like connectivity cables and energy pipelines. Driven by rising concerns over hybrid warfare and sabotage, these efforts leverage rapid advancements in artificial intelligence, drone technology, and autonomous surveillance systems to monitor the ocean floor.

stories.headline: India forces caller-ID apps to feed spam reports to telcos
stories.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has updated its anti-spam rules to mandate that caller-ID and call-management apps share user-reported spam data with telecom operators. This data must be sent to a blockchain-based platform maintained by telcos to track commercial communications and enforce anti-spam regulations. Truecaller has criticized the decision as anti-competitive, arguing it forces the company to hand over a commercially valuable proprietary asset to telecom operators.
